title: Aggressive Cows
description:
You are given an array `stalls` of `n` distinct integer positions representing the locations of stalls along a straight line (not necessarily in sorted order), and an integer `cows` representing the number of aggressive cows to place in the stalls.

To keep the cows from fighting, you want to assign each cow to a stall such that the minimum distance between any two cows is as large as possible. Return the largest possible minimum distance between any two cows.
constraints: All values in stalls are distinct.
hints: Sort the stall positions first so distances between consecutive placed cows are easy to measure.
For a candidate minimum distance d, greedily place the first cow at stalls[0] and each subsequent cow at the earliest stall at least d units away from the previous cow.
If placing all cows at distance d is feasible, every smaller distance is also feasible. Binary search for the largest feasible d in [1, stalls[-1] - stalls[0]].

examples.explanation: After sorting to [1, 2, 4, 8, 9], placing 3 cows at stalls 1, 4, and 8 (or 1, 4, and 9) yields a minimum distance of 3.
Placing 3 cows at stalls 1, 4, and 7 gives pairwise distances 3, 3, and 6, so the minimum distance is 3.
With 2 cows, place them at the extreme stalls 1 and 1000000000 for a distance of 999999999.

timeComplexity: O(n log n + n log D)
